newAPIsTested.errorMessage: Needs TWO INDEPENDENTLY CREATED addresses, and is DESTRUCTIVE AND NOT IDEMPOTENT. The producer POST /api/geo/canonicalize captures exactly one address_id (geo.canonicalize.response.data.address.address_id), so an automated case could only pass the same id as winner and loser - which the handler does not block and which self-deletes the row, destroying the address the sibling geo definitions read. Merge also deletes the loser, so a replay 404s the second time and the case could never be re-run. The payload therefore takes operator-supplied {{var:geo_winner_address_id}} / {{var:geo_loser_address_id}} rather than a cache ref. This is a TWO-PRODUCER plus destructive-replay limitation, not a missing payload or an uncaptured path param - it is not the case MUST-49 forbids marking manual.

newAPIsTested.errorMessage: TENANT-ISOLATION LIMIT, not a missing payload or an uncaptured path param. Candidate links are raised only inside the probabilistic matcher (empiService.matchAndLink) — there is no HTTP write path that creates one — so the only reviewable link is a SEEDED fixture. The handler takes tenant_id from the JWT and deliberately NOT from the body (routes.ts: 'a body-supplied tenant would let a caller' cross the boundary), while this suite signs up a FRESH tenant on every run. The two fixtures therefore cannot both be true: empi_seed_candidate_link.sql stamps its link with the fixed tenant e22662dc-7e65-472a-a6da-41d59163714a, which a newly created tenant cannot see, and the older 11111111-1111-1111-1111-111111111111 row carries tenant_id NULL, which the tenant-scoped read excludes by construction — the seed's own comment says an unstamped fixture 'would be invisible to every caller'. Both were verified present in the local database and both are correctly invisible, which is why this returned 404 CandidateLinkNotFound rather than anything fixable in the definition. Making it auto needs either a stable QA tenant credential (none exists in test-config and no definition authenticates as a fixed tenant) or an HTTP route that raises a candidate link for the calling tenant. Covered meanwhile by seeding and calling it as the fixture tenant by hand. NOTE: {{var:link_id}} resolves to the tenant-NULL row, so it points at the one fixture that can never be returned; if a stable-tenant credential is ever added, repoint it at 0e3b1a70-0000-4000-8000-00000000e001 as well.

testCases._blocked: UNREACHABLE with the current dependency model, and deliberately left failing rather than papered over. satisfyClock() checks SATISFIABLE_STATES and throws InvalidClockTransition (409) BEFORE it evaluates evidence kinds (422). Every dataset here shares one clock_id, and the producer dataset satisfies that clock first, so this case can only ever reach the state check. Proving the 422 needs a second, still-open clock — which MUST-51 cannot express, because its dependency graph is one node per METHOD+ENDPOINT and POST /api/sla/clocks is already that node. Changing expectedStatus to 409 would make it green while testing the already-satisfied path that dataset [2] already covers, i.e. asserting nothing. The evidence-kind rule is covered by the sdk-sla unit tests instead.
testCases.description: MUST RUN BEFORE the successful satisfy: all datasets share one clock ({{cache:sla.clock.create.response.data.clock.clock_id}}), and once it is satisfied the route answers 409 TRANSITION_CONFLICT before it ever validates the evidence kind — so this 422 case can only be observed while the clock is still open. The 409 case that follows the satisfy depends on the same ordering from the other side.

This definition was authored against an endpoint that was never built, so it can only ever return 404 "Route GET:/api/role-templates not found" — confirmed in the prod run. skippedTests.errorMessage: TENANT-ISOLATION LIMIT, not a missing payload or an uncaptured path param. Candidate links are raised only inside the probabilistic matcher (empiService.matchAndLink) — there is no HTTP write path that creates one — so the only reviewable link is a SEEDED fixture. The handler takes tenant_id from the JWT and deliberately NOT from the body (routes.ts: 'a body-supplied tenant would let a caller' cross the boundary), while this suite signs up a FRESH tenant on every run. The two fixtures therefore cannot both be true: empi_seed_candidate_link.sql stamps its link with the fixed tenant e22662dc-7e65-472a-a6da-41d59163714a, which a newly created tenant cannot see, and the older 11111111-1111-1111-1111-111111111111 row carries tenant_id NULL, which the tenant-scoped read excludes by construction — the seed's own comment says an unstamped fixture 'would be invisible to every caller'. Both were verified present in the local database and both are correctly invisible, which is why this returned 404 CandidateLinkNotFound rather than anything fixable in the definition. Making it auto needs either a stable QA tenant credential (none exists in test-config and no definition authenticates as a fixed tenant) or an HTTP route that raises a candidate link for the calling tenant. Covered meanwhile by seeding and calling it as the fixture tenant by hand. NOTE: {{var:link_id}} resolves to the tenant-NULL row, so it points at the one fixture that can never be returned; if a stable-tenant credential is ever added, repoint it at 0e3b1a70-0000-4000-8000-00000000e001 as well.
